text:
evan: Heads up — I'm planning an RBAC tweak for private deployments tomorrow 07:30 UTC. Need a quick flight-check on KMS access, audit logging, and isolation guarantees before we roll. :eyes:

tara: What specifically are you changing? any svc accounts losing kms:Decrypt?

ev an: typo — evan. Proposal: narrow `redwood-private-controller` role: revoke broad `kms:*` and grant only `kms:Decrypt` scoped to per-tenant CMKs and require encryption context. Also deny `kms:GenerateDataKey*` from that role. Goal is reduce blast radius for stolen controller creds.

priyanka: +1 on least-priv. Couple notes: audit must capture KMS key id, principal, and encryptionContext (tenant_id). We should forward `kms:Decrypt` events to our SIEM and add a checksum of request payload to detect replay. Suggested CloudAudit filter: `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt"` (adapt for AWS/GCP).

dmitri: Network side: for on-prem private deployments we must enforce egress isolation. Plan: default-deny egress at pod level, only allow to our KMS gateway IPs over mTLS port (443) and to the internal NAT for package repos. Example NetworkPolicy snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-kms
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: ["Egress"]
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.8.240.0/28 # kms-gateway subnet
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

ops-alex: How do we roll this without breaking live controllers? If we revoke `GenerateDataKey` we might break key rotation jobs. Need a canary: patch role in staging cluster, run `make smoke-decrypt` which runs `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey` checks. Also schedule 15m maintenance window.

sec-bot: automated-scan: HIGH - found exposed key material on jumpbox: `/home/ops/.ssh/authorized_keys` used by `ops-jenkins` contains an AWS key pair with `kms:*` scope. Evidence attached to ticket #INC-2026-894. Recommend immediate revocation. :rotating_light:

priyanka: Ack. Immediate actions I recommend: 1) revoke the exposed creds now, 2) rotate the affected CMK ARN (create new key and grant decrypt to controller role with encryptionContext restriction), 3) snapshot the jumpbox for forensics, 4) enable `kms:Decrypt` alerts in SIEM with high severity, 5) apply new RBAC role with `Condition`/`Context` that includes `tenant_id` check. I can take 1+2.

dmitri: For on-prem KMS (HSM) we also need to confirm mTLS client cert rotation cadence (30 days) and that the agent validates server cert by SPKI pinning; otherwise a compromised internal CA could proxy requests.

ev an: I'll own coordinating the rollout. Plan: 07:30 UTC staging canary, 08:00 UTC production gradual 5% -> 30% -> 100% over 45m, post-checks at each step (smoke decrypt, app health, audit event counts). Priya take key rotation, Alex run the canary steps, Dima verify network policy enforcement and cert pins.

tara: In addition to SIEM alerts, can we add a short-term audit sink that retains raw decrypt logs for 90 days in cold storage? That would help triage if something was exfiltrated.

priyanka: Yes — create a signed, append-only bucket with restricted read and grant only sec-mfa role access. Will add lifecycle rule to move to Glacier/Archive after 30 days.

ops-alex: I'll draft the rollout playbook and include rollback: immediately restore old role bindings and revoke newly created keys if any downstream failure > 5% error rate. Also will add feature-flag to controllers to use cached keys for 3m to avoid transient failures.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-894 created and linked: https://tracker.redwood/INC-2026-894 — severity: high, assigned: priyanka, ops-alex.

oncall-bot: Reminder: if we rotate CMKs, schedule key replication window for DR region (90m).

ev an: Thanks team. If nobody objects I'll start the patch tomorrow. Please ack in-thread when you've completed your pre-roll checks. :thumbsup:
